content:
Rakhi marketing is usually all about one question: “What are you gifting your sibling?”

IGP asked a much more interesting one: “Which memory with your sibling would you put on a billboard?” ❤️

Their latest campaign lets you turn a personal sibling moment into part of the outdoor campaign.

Just scan the QR code or use the WhatsApp link, share a picture with your sibling, and add your Rakhi message.

That’s it.

Your personal memory could then get its own moment on a real billboard. 🥹

From a marketing perspective, I love this because the brand isn’t just showcasing a product.

It is giving people a reason to participate.

And that makes the campaign feel less like an advertisement and more like a celebration of the relationship itself.

Because every sibling relationship has its own story the childhood fights, silly memories, endless teasing, and the quiet support that never needs to be announced. 😂❤️

So this Rakhi, IGP didn’t just ask us to celebrate our siblings.

They gave us a chance to put that bond in the spotlight.

And honestly, that’s a pretty cool way to celebrate Rakhi. ✨
comment: The interesting shift is turning customers into storytellers rather than just buyers. The challenge for brands will be preserving that authenticity at scale while managing privacy and participation expectations.
